definition_zh: 意识到的；知道的；有警觉的；有……意识的
definition_en: knowing or noticing that something exists, is happening, or matters, and being alert to it
core_image: 暗处忽然亮起的一盏灯：原本关闭的感知被点亮，周围的一切变得可见
scene: On the night hike, the guide stopped and asked the group whether everyone was aware of the steep drop just beyond the trail.
sceneCN: 这里 aware 是「对风险有认知」（第 8 个义项：对风险有认知）；句意：夜行途中，向导停下来，问大家是否都意识到步道外就是陡坡。图中可辨识物件：头灯、步道边缘、陡坡、登山队、向导的手势。

derivatives.zh: 不知道的；没有意识到的

senses.title: Knowledge of something: aware of
senses.definition: having knowledge that something exists or is present, usually through noticing or being told
senses.definitionCN: 知道某事物存在或出现，通常源于察觉或被告知
senses.example: She was aware of a faint smell of smoke in the hallway.
senses.exampleCN: 她察觉到走廊里有一丝烟味。
senses.why: The Old English base wær meant 'watchful, on guard'. To be aware of something is to have your watchfulness switched on and that thing inside its light, so knowledge begins as a kind of noticing rather than as stored information.
senses.whyCN: 古英语词干 wær 意为“警觉的、处于看守状态的”。be aware of 某物，就是让你的警觉被打开、让那件东西进入这盏灯的光圈，所以这里的“知道”起点是“察觉”，而非脑子里存着一条资料。

senses.title: Knowing a fact: aware that
senses.definition: knowing a particular fact, often because it has been said or reported to you
senses.definitionCN: 知道某一具体事实，常因别人说过或告知过
senses.example: Are you aware that the deadline has been moved to Friday?
senses.exampleCN: 你知道截止日期已经改到周五了吗？
senses.why: The that-clause turns the watchfulness toward a whole proposition rather than a thing. The same inner light now falls on a fact, so 'aware' moves from sensing an object to holding a piece of knowledge.
senses.whyCN: that 从句把“警觉的目光”从一件东西转向一整个命题。同一盏内在的灯现在照在一个事实之上，于是 aware 从“感觉到某个对象”延伸为“掌握一条信息”。

senses.title: Watchful of surroundings: alert
senses.definition: alert and attentive to what is happening around you, especially in order to avoid danger
senses.definitionCN: 对周围发生的事情保持警觉和注意，尤为避免危险
senses.example: Cyclists should be especially aware near busy intersections.
senses.exampleCN: 骑行者在大交叉路口附近尤其应当保持警觉。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of wær: the guard who keeps watching the road. The word still carries that physical vigilance, so 'aware' can describe a steady state of scanning rather than a single realization.
senses.whyCN: 这是 wær 最古老的一层：看守者一直盯着路口。这个词至今保留那种身体性的警戒，所以 aware 可以指持续的“扫视状态”，而不只是一次“恍然大悟”。

senses.title: Self-aware: observing oneself
senses.definition: conscious of your own character, feelings, or effect on other people
senses.definitionCN: 对自己的性格、情绪或给他人的影响有清醒认识
senses.example: He is self-aware enough to admit that his joke upset her.
senses.exampleCN: 他有足够的自我认识，承认自己的玩笑让她难过了。
senses.why: The light of wær is turned around and pointed at the self. The same watchfulness that once guarded against outside danger now guards against your own blind spots, which is why self- is the prefix that creates this branch.
senses.whyCN: wær 的灯光被调转方向照向自己。原本用于防备外界危险的警觉，现在用来防备自己的盲点，所以这一支由 self- 前缀构成。

senses.title: Social or political consciousness
senses.definition: informed about and attentive to social or political issues, often with a sense of responsibility
senses.definitionCN: 对社会或政治议题有了解且持续关注，常带责任感
senses.example: Politically aware voters ask where the money for a promise will come from.
senses.exampleCN: 有政治意识的选民会追问一项承诺的钱从哪里来。
senses.why: Awareness here widens from a private watch to a public one. The 'watchful' sense is applied to the whole society, so the word stops meaning 'I see this' and starts meaning 'I see what this costs everyone'.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 awareness 从私人的看守扩展为公共的看守。“警觉”被用在整个社会上，于是这个词不再只是“我看见这件事”，而开始表示“我看见这件事对所有人意味着什么”。

senses.title: Faint perception: half-aware
senses.definition: having a partial or unclear perception of something that is not yet fully identified
senses.definitionCN: 对尚未完全辨认的事物只有部分、模糊的感知
senses.example: Half asleep, he was aware of a presence at the foot of the bed.
senses.exampleCN: 半睡半醒间，他模糊感觉到床尾有个影子。
senses.why: Watchfulness can be dim as well as bright. The lamp is only half on, so the thing is registered without being clearly named; this is why 'aware' allows degree (faintly aware, half aware).
senses.whyCN: 警觉的灯既可全亮也可半亮。灯只开了一半，东西被记录下来却没有被清楚命名；因此 aware 允许程度修饰（faintly aware、half aware）。

senses.title: Environmental awareness
senses.definition: conscious of the environmental impact of choices and acting with that knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 意识到各种选择对环境的影响，并据此行动
senses.example: Environmentally aware shoppers bring their own bags and avoid single-use plastic.
senses.exampleCN: 有环保意识的购物者自带袋子，避免一次性塑料制品。
senses.why: The old watchfulness is now aimed at consequences that are distant in time and space. What you cannot see directly still stays inside the light, so awareness becomes a moral habit rather than a reflex.
senses.whyCN: 古老的警觉现在对准了在时间和空间上都很遥远的后果。看不见的影响仍被留在光圈里，于是 awareness 从反射式的察觉变成一种道德习惯。

senses.title: Risk-aware: knowing the danger
senses.definition: recognizing a specific danger and understanding what could follow from it
senses.definitionCN: 识别出具体危险，并理解它可能带来的后果
senses.example: Risk-aware investors read the warning section before they sign.
senses.exampleCN: 有风险意识的投资者会在签字前阅读警示部分。
senses.why: This is the guard's function made explicit: wær sees the threat and stays awake to it. The compound risk-aware keeps both halves visible — the danger outside, the watchfulness inside.
senses.whyCN: 这是“看守”功能最直白的版本：wær 看见威胁并持续警醒。risk-aware 这个复合词把两半都摆明——外面是危险，里面是警觉。

senses.title: Clear-headed: mentally awake
senses.definition: mentally alert and responding normally, not dazed or confused
senses.definitionCN: 神志清醒、反应正常，不恍惚、不糊涂
senses.example: The driver was shaken but fully aware when the paramedics arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 急救人员赶到时，司机虽受惊但完全清醒。
senses.why: The light metaphor reaches its most literal point here: aware means the mind is lit up, not fogged. The Old English sense 'watchful' becomes 'awake to the world' in the medical and everyday use.
senses.whyCN: “灯”的比喻在这里最接近字面：aware 意为脑子是亮的，不是起雾的。古英语的“警觉”在医学和日常用法里变成了“对世界保持醒着”。

intro.en: Aware comes from Old English gewær, a prefixed adjective whose prefix later dropped away. The derivation chain is ge- (completive/collective) + wær 'watchful' → aware, and modern English then re-prefixes it with un-, self- and hyper-.
intro.cn: aware 来自古英语 gewær，是一个带前缀的形容词，后来前缀脱落。派生链为 ge-（完成／集合前缀）+ wær“警觉的”→ aware；现代英语再用 un-、self-、hyper- 重新给它加前缀。

items.en: The source is gewær 'watchful, alert, cautious'. The first element ge- was a completive or collective prefix, and the second was wær 'watchful, on guard'. The word therefore began as a state: having one's guard fully up.
items.cn: 来源是 gewær“警觉的、留神的、谨慎的”。第一个成分 ge- 是完成或集合前缀，第二个成分是 wær“警觉的、处于看守状态的”。所以这个词最初是一种状态：警戒完全打开。

items.en: The ge- prefix fell away, leaving awarre and then aware. The meaning 'watchful, cautious' survived, and the modern spelling settled as aware.
items.cn: ge- 前缀脱落，先留下 awarre，再变成 aware。含义“警觉的、谨慎的”保留下来，现代拼写固定为 aware。

items.en: The construction be aware of became established, and 'aware of' grew common in the 17th century. The word shifted from a standing trait ('a wary person') to a live event ('a person who has noticed something').
items.cn: be aware of 结构确立，“aware of”在 17 世纪开始流行。这个词从一种长期特质（“一个谨慎的人”）转向一次当下的动作（“一个刚刚注意到某事的人”）。

items.en: wær is reconstructed as Proto-Germanic *waraz 'wary, watchful', related to *warōn 'to guard, watch'. The same family gives English ward, warn, wary and beware, which is why they all involve keeping watch.
items.cn: wær 被重构为原始日耳曼语 *waraz“谨慎的、警觉的”，与 *warōn“看守、警戒”相关。同一词族产生英语 ward、warn、wary、beware，所以它们都含有“看守”的意思。

items.en: The family is generally traced to PIE *wer- 'to watch, guard, heed'. The deeper connections of this root to other PIE branches are not fully certain, so the chain stops reliably at 'watch/guard'.
items.cn: 该词族一般追溯到原始印欧语 *wer-“看守、警觉、留意”。这个词根与其他印欧语支的更深联系并不完全确定，因此可靠的链条止于“看守／警觉”。

items.en: English treats aware as a productive base: un- + aware → unaware, aware + -ness → awareness, self- + aware → self-aware, hyper- + aware → hyperaware. The meaning also widens from physical watchfulness to social, political, environmental and medical consciousness.
items.cn: 现代英语把 aware 当作能产的基础词：un- + aware → unaware，aware + -ness → awareness，self- + aware → self-aware，hyper- + aware → hyperaware。词义也从身体性的警觉扩展到社会、政治、环保和医学意识。

note.en: The first group lists words that look or sound close to aware; the second lists words that share its meaning. Form comes first, then meaning.
note.cn: 第一组列出与 aware 形音相近的词；第二组列出意思相近的词。先看词形，再看词义。

entries.definition: not asleep; also used figuratively for being alert. It shares the aw- opening but comes from a different verb, 'to wake'.
entries.definitionCN: 醒着的；也可比喻为警觉的。它同样以 aw- 开头，但来自另一个动词“醒来”。

entries.definition: to be cautious of a danger. It is be- + ware, and ware is the same watchful base that gave aware.
entries.definitionCN: 当心、提防危险。它是 be- + ware，而 ware 正是产生 aware 的那个“警觉”词干。

entries.definition: cautious because of possible danger. It keeps the original wær meaning more directly than aware does.
entries.definitionCN: 因可能有危险而谨慎的。它比 aware 更直接地保留了 wær 的本义。

entries.definition: awake and able to perceive, or aware of something. It is broader and more neutral than aware.
entries.definitionCN: 醒着并能感知的，或意识到某事的。它比 aware 更宽泛、更中性。

entries.definition: carefully aware of something and keeping it in mind, often with a caring tone.
entries.definitionCN: 细心意识到某事并把它放在心上，常带关怀意味。

entries.definition: formally aware or informed, used in law and business. It sounds more official than aware.
entries.definitionCN: 正式地知道或知情，多用于法律和商务。它比 aware 更带公文语气。

entries.definition: quick to notice and react to danger. It stresses reaction speed, while aware stresses knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 对危险能迅速注意并作出反应。它强调反应速度，而 aware 强调知道。

entries.definition: having facts or background knowledge. It focuses on information held rather than on perception.
entries.definitionCN: 掌握事实或背景知识。它侧重拥有的信息，而非当下的感知。

normalIntro.en: These work with the real parts and real relatives of aware: the dropped ge- prefix, the wær base, and the modern un-/self-/hyper- family.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都用 aware 真实的成分和同族词：脱落了的 ge- 前缀、wær 词干，以及现代的 un-/self-/hyper- 词族。

normal.en: gewær = ge- + wær. The ge- prefix is gone, but the 'fully switched on' sense is still inside aware.
normal.cn: gewær = ge- + wær。ge- 前缀虽然消失了，但“完全打开”的感觉仍留在 aware 里面。

normal.en: wær is the same base as wary, warn, ward and beware: all of them involve keeping watch.
normal.cn: wær 与 wary、warn、ward、beware 同源：它们都含有“看守”的意思。

normal.en: Aware of is the everyday frame; aware that adds a full fact after it.
normal.cn: aware of 是日常框架；aware that 后面接一整个事实。

normal.en: Self-aware turns the watch inward: you guard against your own blind spots.
normal.cn: self-aware 把看守转向内部：你提防的是自己的盲点。

normal.en: Unaware and awareness show how freely English re-prefixes and suffixes the word.
normal.cn: unaware 与 awareness 说明英语可以自由地给这个词加前缀和后缀。

abstract.en: Imagine a lamp in a dark room. Off means unaware; half-lit means faintly aware; fully on means clearly aware.
abstract.cn: 想象昏暗房间里的一盏灯。关着是 unaware；半亮是 faintly aware；全亮是 clearly aware。

abstract.en: The guard at the gate is the original image: aware means the guard is awake inside you, watching the road.
abstract.cn: 门口的看守是最初的意象：aware 意味着你内部那个看守醒着，盯着路口。

abstract.en: The same light can point outward at danger, inward at the self, or across society at shared problems.
abstract.cn: 同一盏灯可以朝外照危险，朝内照自己，也可以横跨社会照共同的问题。

examples.en: She became aware of a quiet footstep behind her.
examples.cn: 她察觉到身后有轻轻的脚步声。

examples.en: Few people are aware that the museum closes at four on Sundays.
examples.cn: 很少有人知道博物馆周日四点闭馆。

examples.en: A good teacher is aware of how much silence a nervous student needs.
examples.cn: 好老师能察觉一个紧张的学生需要多少沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: “啊，喂！”——有人在暗处喊了一声“啊，喂！”，你这才意识到身边有人 → aware 意识到、察觉

root: 古英语 gewær“警觉的、留神的”，ge- 为完成/集合前缀 + wær“警觉”，与 ward、warn、wary、beware 同出 PIE *wer-“看守、警觉”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of aware all grow from one image: a watchlight that can be bright or dim, pointed outward at things and facts, inward at the self, or across society at risks and responsibilities.
sensesIntro.cn: aware 的九个义项都生长自同一个意象：一盏警觉的灯，可以亮可以暗，可以朝外照事物和事实，朝内照自己，也可以横跨社会照风险与责任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a watchlight switches on and the thing in front of it becomes visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏警觉的灯被打开，灯前的东西因此变得可见。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE: an object or a fact enters the light, so awareness becomes knowing that something is there or true.
branches.cn: 知识：一个对象或一个事实进入光圈，awareness 于是成为“知道某物存在或为真”。

branches.en: PERCEPTION: the light can burn steadily (alert) or only half-light a shape (faint awareness); both are degrees of watchfulness.
branches.cn: 感知：灯可以稳定长明（警觉），也可以只半照出一个轮廓（模糊察觉）；两者都是警觉的程度。

branches.en: SELF: the beam turns inward, and watchfulness becomes self-observation.
branches.cn: 自我：光束转向内部，警觉变成自我观察。

branches.en: SOCIETY: the same light widens to political and environmental consequences that lie beyond direct sight.
branches.cn: 社会：同一盏灯扩展到政治与环保后果，那些后果超出直接视野。

branches.en: DANGER AND CLARITY: the guard sees the threat and stays awake, and in its most literal form aware means the mind is not fogged.
branches.cn: 危险与清醒：看守看见威胁并保持醒着；在最字面的用法里，aware 指头脑没有起雾。

intro.en: Aware is not built from a living Latin prefix. Its original ge- prefix has disappeared, and modern English builds new words with un-, self- and hyper- plus the suffix -ness.
intro.cn: aware 不是由活的拉丁前缀构成的。它原有的 ge- 前缀已经消失；现代英语用 un-、self-、hyper- 加上后缀 -ness 来造新词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin branch for aware: the word is Germanic all the way down to PIE *wer- 'to watch'. The meaningful relatives are English ward, warn, wary and beware, not Latin roots.
latinIntro.cn: aware 没有拉丁语分支：这个词一路是日耳曼语，直到 PIE *wer-“看守”。有意义的同族词是英语的 ward、warn、wary、beware，而不是拉丁词根。

items.meaning: the state of knowing or noticing something
items.meaningCN: 意识；认识；察觉（-ness 构成状态名词）
items.example: Public awareness of the water shortage grew quickly.
items.exampleCN: 公众对缺水的意识迅速提高。

items.meaning: not knowing or not realizing something
items.meaningCN: 不知道的；没有意识到的（un- 表否定）
items.example: He was unaware that the train had been cancelled.
items.exampleCN: 他不知道那班火车已经取消。

items.meaning: lack of awareness; the state of not knowing
items.meaningCN: 无意识；不知情（否定前缀加状态后缀）
items.example: Her unawareness of the new rule caused a delay.
items.exampleCN: 她不知道新规定，导致了延误。

items.meaning: without being prepared; unexpectedly
items.meaningCN: 出其不意地；冷不防地（-s 构成副词）
items.example: The rain caught us unawares.
items.exampleCN: 那场雨让我们措手不及。

items.meaning: conscious of one's own character and effect
items.meaningCN: 有自我意识的（self- 把对象转向自身）
items.example: A self-aware manager knows when to stop talking.
items.exampleCN: 有自我意识的管理者知道什么时候该闭嘴。

items.meaning: the ability to observe one's own thoughts and behaviour
items.meaningCN: 自我意识；自我认识（self- 加 -ness）
items.example: Writing a journal can build self-awareness.
items.exampleCN: 写日记可以培养自我认识。

items.meaning: excessively conscious of something
items.meaningCN: 过度意识的；过分敏感的（hyper- 表过度）
items.example: Teenagers can become hyperaware of their appearance.
items.exampleCN: 青少年可能对自己的外貌过度敏感。

items.meaning: an excessive, often anxious state of noticing
items.meaningCN: 过度警觉；过分在意（hyper- 加 -ness）
items.example: Hyperawareness of every glance made the interview painful.
items.exampleCN: 对每个眼神都过分在意，让面试变得难受。

definition_zh: 家庭的；家用的；本国的；国内的；家养的
definition_en: relating to the home or family, or to one's own country rather than to foreign countries
core_image: 一圈围住炉火的墙：墙内是家，墙外是别处；同一个“家”的尺度可以放大到整个国家
scene: At the airport, the departures board lists domestic flights on the left and international flights on the right, and her flight to Lhasa appears on the left.
sceneCN: 这里 domestic 是「国内航班」（第 4 个义项：在国内运行的航班／线路）；句意：机场的出发牌把航班分成国内和国际两类，她飞往拉萨的航班列在国内一侧。图中可辨识物件：航班信息屏、登机口、行李箱、国内／国际分区标识、旅客。

pos.zh: 家政工人；家仆（旧时用法）

derivatives.zh: 已驯化的；适应家庭生活的

senses.title: Of the home: household and family
senses.definition: relating to the home, the household, or family life
senses.definitionCN: 与家、家庭或家庭生活有关的
senses.example: The survey asks about domestic chores and childcare.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查询问家务和育儿情况。
senses.why: Latin domus is simply 'house', and the suffix -ticus turns it into an adjective meaning 'of the house'. This sense is the plainest use of that adjective: everything that happens inside the walls of a home.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 domus 就是“房子”，后缀 -ticus 把它变成形容词“房子的”。这个义项是那个形容词最朴素的用法：发生在家庭围墙之内的一切。

senses.title: Of one's own country: national
senses.definition: relating to one's own country rather than to foreign countries
senses.definitionCN: 与本国的而非外国的有关的
senses.example: The president spent the morning on domestic affairs.
senses.exampleCN: 总统整个上午都在处理国内事务。
senses.why: A nation is imagined as a very large household: the same domus adjective is stretched from the family house to the national house. The meaning did not come from a new root but from a metaphor of scale.
senses.whyCN: 国家被想象成一个放大的家：同一个 domus 形容词从家庭住宅被拉伸到国家这座“大房子”。这个意思不是来自新词根，而是来自尺度的比喻。

senses.title: Of the house: tamed animals
senses.definition: kept by people as a pet or farm animal rather than living wild
senses.definitionCN: 由人饲养作宠物或农畜，而非野生
senses.example: Domestic cats have lived alongside humans for thousands of years.
senses.exampleCN: 家猫与人类共同生活了数千年。
senses.why: An animal that is literally 'of the house' stands on the inside of the wall, while the wild animal stands outside it. Domestic is therefore a spatial label before it is a biological one.
senses.whyCN: 字面“属于房子”的动物站在墙的内侧，野生动物站在墙的外侧。因此 domestic 首先是一个空间标签，其次才是生物学标签。

senses.title: Within the country: domestic flights and routes
senses.titleCN: 在国内运行的：国内航班与线路
senses.definition: operating or travelling inside a country's borders, without crossing into another country
senses.definitionCN: 在一国境内运行或旅行，不越过国界进入他国
senses.example: She booked a domestic flight from Chengdu to Lhasa.
senses.exampleCN: 她订了一张从成都到拉萨的国内航班。
senses.why: The nation is again the house, and a flight that stays inside it never crosses the wall. International begins exactly where the domestic route ends, so the prefix domestic- marks the inside of the border.
senses.whyCN: 国家再次是那座房子，留在里面的航班从不越过围墙。国际正好从国内航线的终点开始，所以 domestic 标记的是国界的内侧。

senses.title: Internal affairs: domestic policy
senses.definition: concerned with a country's own internal government and politics
senses.definitionCN: 涉及一国自身的内部治理与政治
senses.example: Domestic policy is often harder to sell than foreign policy.
senses.exampleCN: 国内政策往往比外交政策更难推销。
senses.why: Affairs 'of the house' are the ones conducted inside the national walls. Once the nation is treated as a household, taxes, health and education become domestic matters while war and trade lie outside.
senses.whyCN: “房子里的”事务就是在国家围墙内处理的事务。一旦国家被当作家庭，税收、医疗和教育就成了 domestic 事务，而战争与贸易则位于墙外。

senses.title: Household servant: a domestic
senses.definition: a person employed to work in a private house, especially in cleaning or cooking
senses.definitionCN: 受雇在私宅工作的人，尤指负责清洁或烹饪
senses.example: The estate employed a staff of ten domestics.
senses.exampleCN: 这座庄园雇了十名家政工人。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun by ellipsis: a domestic servant, shortened to a domestic. The person is named by the space they work in, so the house itself defines the job.
senses.whyCN: 形容词通过省略变成名词：a domestic servant 缩略成 a domestic。人被其工作的空间命名，所以房子本身定义了这份工作。

senses.title: The market inside the border
senses.definition: the market existing within a country, as opposed to export markets abroad
senses.definitionCN: 存在于一国境内的市场，相对于国外出口市场
senses.example: Firms that rely only on the domestic market tend to grow slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 只依赖国内市场的公司往往增长缓慢。
senses.why: The national house has an inside space, and trade conducted in that space is domestic trade. Exports leave through the wall, so the same house metaphor now separates home sales from foreign sales.
senses.whyCN: 国家这座房子有内部空间，在这个空间里进行的交易就是国内贸易。出口要穿过围墙，所以同一个“房子”比喻现在把国内销售与国外销售分开。

senses.title: Private life inside the home
senses.titleCN: 家庭生活：围墙内的日常
senses.definition: the ordinary private life and atmosphere of a household
senses.definitionCN: 家庭普通的私人生活与氛围
senses.example: The novel is a quiet portrait of domestic life.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是一幅平静的家庭生活画像。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes not objects but a rhythm: meals, chores, children, small routines. Domus as 'home' rather than 'building' is what makes this sense warmer and more intimate.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词描述的不是物件，而是一种节奏：吃饭、家务、孩子、小小的日常。domus 作为“家”而不是“建筑”，使这个义项更温暖、更亲密。

senses.title: Violence inside the household
senses.titleCN: 家庭暴力：发生在围墙内的伤害
senses.definition: violence or abuse between members of the same household
senses.definitionCN: 同一家庭成员之间的暴力或虐待
senses.example: Police recorded a rise in domestic violence during the lockdown.
senses.exampleCN: 封控期间，警方记录的家庭暴力案件有所上升。
senses.why: Domus should be the safest enclosure, yet the adjective here marks harm that happens inside it. The same wall that defines the home also defines where the abuse can be hidden, so the root's protective image turns into a trap.
senses.whyCN: domus 本应是最安全的围合空间，但这里的形容词标记的是发生在它内部的伤害。定义家的那堵墙，也定义了虐待可以被藏在哪里，于是词根的保护意象反过来成了牢笼。

intro.en: Domestic is a Latin adjective of the house that English borrowed through French. The chain is domus 'house' + -ticus → domesticus → French domestique → English domestic; later suffixes build domesticate, domestication, domesticity and domestically, and the sense moves from the family house to the nation.
intro.cn: domestic 是一个经由法语进入英语的拉丁“房子”形容词。派生链为 domus“房子”+ -ticus → domesticus → 法语 domestique → 英语 domestic；后来再加后缀产生 domesticate、domestication、domesticity、domestically，词义也从家庭住宅扩展到国家。

items.en: domus is generally traced to PIE *dem- 'house, household' (sometimes written *dom-). Cognates include Greek domos and Sanskrit dama-, and the 'house' sense is widely accepted; the exact shape of the deeper root is a reconstruction, not a recorded form.
items.cn: domus 一般追溯到原始印欧语 *dem-“房子、家户”（有时写作 *dom-）。同源词包括希腊语 domos 和梵语 dama-；“房子”这一义项被广泛接受，但更深词根的具体形态是重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Latin domus means 'house, home, household'. The adjective domesticus is domus + -ticus, an adjectival suffix of belonging, parallel to rusticus 'of the country'. So domesticus starts as a plain possessive: 'belonging to the house'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 domus 意为“房子、家、家户”。形容词 domesticus = domus + -ticus，-ticus 是表示归属的形容词后缀，与 rusticus“乡下的”平行。因此 domesticus 起初只是朴素的所属关系：“属于这座房子的”。

items.en: English records domestic in the 1520s, borrowed from Middle French domestique. The early sense is 'belonging to the home'; the national sense ('of one's own country') is also early, built on the same metaphor of the nation as a household.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 20 年代记录到 domestic，借自中古法语 domestique。早期义为“属于家的”；“本国的”这一国家义也很早出现，建立在同一个“国家即家户”的比喻上。

items.en: The adjective is used as a noun for a household servant, and domestic animal becomes the standard label for tamed species. Domesticity names the quality or state of home life. These uses all keep the literal domus inside them.
items.cn: 这个形容词被名词化，指家政仆役；domestic animal 成为驯化物种的标准说法。domesticity 指家庭生活的性质或状态。这些用法内部都保留着字面的 domus。

items.en: Fixed modern collocations appear: domestic flight, domestic market, gross domestic product, domestic violence. The word now shifts freely between the house and the nation, and the listener picks the scale from the noun beside it.
items.cn: 现代固定搭配出现：domestic flight、domestic market、gross domestic product、domestic violence。这个词现在在“家”与“国”之间自由切换，听者根据旁边的名词判断尺度。

items.en: Domestic + -ate gives domesticate 'to make tame or home-like'; + -ation gives domestication; + -ity gives domesticity; + -ally gives domestically. The semantic chain is house → household life → one's own country → internal affairs and markets, with the nation always pictured as an enlarged home.
items.cn: domestic + -ate 产生 domesticate“驯化、使居家化”；+ -ation 产生 domestication；+ -ity 产生 domesticity；+ -ally 产生 domestically。语义链是：房子 → 家庭生活 → 本国 → 内政与国内市场，国家始终被想象成一个放大的家。

note.en: The look-alikes share the dom- shape but not always the same root; the near meanings split by scale — house, country, or tamed nature.
note.cn: 形近词共享 dom- 的外形，但未必同根；近义词则按尺度区分——家、国，还是被驯化的自然。

entries.definition: tamed or adapted to home life. It is the past participle of domesticate, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 被驯化的或适应家庭生活的。它是 domesticate 的过去分词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: a formal word for a person's home or usual residence; also a legal term. It comes from the same Latin domus family.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个人的住所或惯常居所的正式词，也是法律术语。它来自同一个拉丁语 domus 词族。

entries.definition: trying to control other people in a bossy way. It begins with dom- but comes from Latin dominus 'lord', a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 专横地试图控制别人。它同样以 dom- 开头，但来自拉丁语 dominus“主人”，是另一个词根。

entries.definition: relating to a home and the people in it. It is more concrete than domestic and rarely means national.
entries.definitionCN: 与家庭及家中的人有关。它比 domestic 更具体，很少表示“国家的”。

entries.definition: relating to a whole nation. It is the direct opposite of 'international' and overlaps domestic only in the country sense.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个国家有关。它是 international 的直接对立面，只在“国家”这一义项上与 domestic 重叠。

entries.definition: situated or happening inside something. It is more spatial and neutral than domestic.
entries.definitionCN: 位于或发生在某物内部的。它比 domestic 更偏空间、更中性。

entries.definition: belonging to a place by birth or origin. It stresses origin, while domestic stresses being inside the border.
entries.definitionCN: 因出生或起源而属于某地。它强调来源，而 domestic 强调位于国界之内。

entries.definition: made calm and obedient around humans. It is the everyday word for the animal sense of domestic.
entries.definitionCN: 在人身边变得温顺听话的。它是 domestic 动物义项的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: These use the real domus family, the -ticus suffix, and the actual collocations that separate the house sense from the nation sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想使用真实的 domus 词族、-ticus 后缀，以及区分“家”与“国”两个义项的真实搭配。

normal.en: domus = house; domesticus = 'of the house'. The whole word begins as a possessive adjective.
normal.cn: domus = 房子；domesticus = “房子的”。整个词起初就是一个表示所属的形容词。

normal.en: The suffix -ticus works like the -ic in rustic: rustic is 'of the country', domestic is 'of the house'.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ticus 就像 rustic 里的 -ic：rustic 是“乡下的”，domestic 是“房子的”。

normal.en: The nation is a giant house: domestic affairs are the affairs inside its walls.
normal.cn: 国家是一所巨大的房子：domestic affairs 就是围墙内的事务。

normal.en: Domestic animals live inside the wall; wild animals live outside it.
normal.cn: domestic animals 生活在墙内；野生动物生活在墙外。

normal.en: Domesticate is domestic + -ate: to bring a wild thing inside the house.
normal.cn: domesticate = domestic + -ate：把野生之物带进房子里。

abstract.en: Picture one wall. Inside it are a stove, a family, chores, pets and private life. Outside it are foreign countries, wild animals and export markets.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙。墙内有炉火、家人、家务、宠物和私人生活；墙外有外国、野生动物和出口市场。

abstract.en: Then zoom out: the same wall is drawn around a whole country, and domestic becomes national.
abstract.cn: 然后把镜头拉远：同一堵墙被画在整个国家周围，domestic 就成了“国家的”。

abstract.en: Zoom in again: the wall that protects can also hide harm, which is how domestic violence gets its chilling name.
abstract.cn: 再把镜头拉近：保护人的墙也能藏住伤害，家庭暴力这个令人心寒的名称就是这样来的。

examples.en: Her domestic duties left her with almost no time to study.
examples.cn: 家务几乎让她没有时间学习。

examples.en: The country's domestic market is small but highly competitive.
examples.cn: 这个国家的国内市场不大，但竞争非常激烈。

examples.en: Domestic dogs often understand far more words than their owners realize.
examples.cn: 家犬听懂的词往往远多于主人以为的。

dict_mnemonic.text: “多美事，待客”——家里最美的事就是招待客人 → domestic 家庭的、家用的

root: 拉丁 domus“房子、家”+ -ticus 形容词后缀 → domesticus“房子的”；经由法语 domestique 进入英语，核心是“属于这个家／这个国界的”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of domestic all come from one wall: inside it are the home, the family, the tamed animal, the servant and private life; when the same wall is drawn around a country, domestic turns into national affairs, routes, policy and markets — and, in its darkest use, the violence hidden inside the home.
sensesIntro.cn: domestic 的九个义项都来自同一堵墙：墙内有家、家人、驯化动物、家仆和私人生活；当同一堵墙被画在整个国家周围，domestic 就变成国内事务、国内航线、国内政策和国内市场——而在最阴暗的用法里，它指藏在家庭内部的暴力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall drawn around a hearth; whatever is inside is domestic, whatever is outside is foreign or wild.
core.cn: 核心意象：围绕炉火画出的墙；墙内的都是 domestic，墙外的则是外国的或野生的。

branches.en: HOME: the plain adjective of the house covers chores, family and the private rhythm of daily life.
branches.cn: 家：最朴素的“房子形容词”涵盖家务、家人和日常私人生活的节奏。

branches.en: NATION: the nation is a household on a larger scale, so its internal affairs and policy become domestic.
branches.cn: 国家：国家是放大尺度的家户，因此它的内部事务和政策成为 domestic。

branches.en: TAMED NATURE: an animal inside the wall is domestic, and the wild is what remains outside.
branches.cn: 被驯化的自然：墙内的动物是家养的，野生的则是留在墙外的东西。

branches.en: INSIDE THE BORDER: flights and markets that stay within the national wall are domestic; crossing the wall makes them international.
branches.cn: 国界之内：留在国家围墙内的航班和市场是 domestic；越过围墙就变成国际的。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND HARM: a servant is named by the house they work in, and the same house can conceal violence behind its protective wall.
branches.cn: 人与伤害：家仆因工作的房子而得名；同一座房子也可能在保护墙后藏住暴力。

intro.en: Domestic is built from a Latin base plus an adjective suffix, and English then adds verb, noun and adverb suffixes to it. The suffixes below are all living or semi-living English endings, not invented parts.
intro.cn: domestic 由拉丁词基加形容词后缀构成，英语随后再加动词、名词和副词后缀。下列后缀都是活的或半活的英语词尾，不是编造的成分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on domus 'house': domesticus 'of the house', domicilium 'dwelling', and the Late Latin verb domesticare 'to bring into the house, tame'. English took the adjective from French and the verb from the same Latin line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族建立在 domus“房子”上：domesticus“房子的”、domicilium“住所”，以及晚期拉丁动词 domesticare“带进家里、驯化”。英语从法语取来形容词，也从同一拉丁线索取来动词。

items.meaning: to tame an animal, or to make something home-like and familiar
items.meaningCN: 驯化动物，或使某物适合家庭、变得熟悉（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: People domesticated wheat over thousands of years.
items.exampleCN: 人类用数千年时间驯化了小麦。

items.meaning: tamed; adapted to living with humans
items.meaningCN: 已驯化的；适应与人类共同生活的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: Domesticated bees produce more honey than wild ones.
items.exampleCN: 已驯化的蜜蜂比野蜂产蜜更多。

items.meaning: the process of taming an animal or plant
items.meaningCN: 驯化；家养化过程（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The domestication of the horse changed transport forever.
items.exampleCN: 马的驯化彻底改变了运输方式。

items.meaning: in or within one's own country; at home
items.meaningCN: 在国内；在家庭方面（-ally 构成副词）
items.example: The company produces all its parts domestically.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司所有零件都在国内生产。

items.meaning: the quality or state of home life
items.meaningCN: 家庭生活；居家氛围（-ity 构成性质或状态名词）
items.example: The play celebrates quiet domesticity rather than adventure.
items.exampleCN: 这部戏赞美的是安静的家庭生活，而不是冒险。

items.meaning: not tamed; still wild
items.meaningCN: 未驯化的；仍是野生的（un- 表否定）
items.example: Undomesticated cats avoid human contact.
items.exampleCN: 未驯化的猫会避开人类接触。

items.meaning: not relating to the home or to one's own country
items.meaningCN: 非家庭的；非本国的（non- 表否定）
items.example: Non-domestic appliances use a different voltage.
items.exampleCN: 非家用的电器使用不同的电压。

items.meaning: the process by which a species adapts itself to life near humans
items.meaningCN: 自我驯化（物种自行适应人类环境的过程）
items.example: Some scientists argue that humans underwent self-domestication.
items.exampleCN: 一些科学家认为人类经历过自我驯化。

latinEntries.meaning: of the house, belonging to the household
to bring into the house; to tame

definition_zh: 利用；剥削；开发；开采；（名词）壮举；漏洞利用程序
definition_en: to use a resource, opportunity or person for profit or advantage; as a noun, a bold achievement, or a piece of code that abuses a software weakness
core_image: 把一张折叠的地图完全摊开，连夹缝里的路都标出来用尽——ex-（向外）+ plicare（折）
scene: The company was accused of trying to exploit a loophole in the new emission rules.
sceneCN: 这里 exploit 是「钻空子」（第 4 个义项：利用规则或系统里的漏洞）；句意：这家公司被指试图钻新排放规则的空子。图中可辨识物件：法规文本、被圈出的条款缝隙、公司标志、律师的手、警示标记。

senses.title: Make full use of a resource or opportunity
senses.definition: to make full use of a resource, opportunity or situation for a purpose or profit
senses.definitionCN: 为某种目的或利益充分利用资源、机会或局面
senses.example: The region has long exploited its vast forests.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区长期以来一直在开发它广阔的森林。
senses.why: Latin explicare is ex- 'out' + plicare 'to fold'. To exploit is to unfold a resource completely and use every part of it. The image is not gentle use but maximum extraction, which is why the word later slid toward 'take advantage'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 explicare 是 ex-“向外”+ plicare“折”。exploit 就是把资源完全摊开、把每一部分都用上。这个意象不是温和地使用，而是最大限度地榨取，所以这个词后来滑向“占便宜”。

senses.title: Take unfair advantage of people's work
senses.definition: to take unfair advantage of someone's work, weakness or need, usually for profit
senses.definitionCN: 为利益不公平地利用他人的劳动、弱点或困境
senses.example: The factory exploited migrant workers with long hours and low pay.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂用超长工时和低工资剥削外来工人。
senses.why: The same 'unfold and use every part' gesture is turned on a person. When the resource is human, complete extraction stops being efficient use and becomes exploitation: the worker is used up rather than fairly employed.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“摊开并用尽每一部分”的动作被转向人。当资源是人时，彻底榨取就不再是高效利用，而成了剥削：工人被用尽，而不是被公平雇用。

senses.title: Develop or extract from land and minerals
senses.definition: to develop land or extract minerals and energy from the ground for profit
senses.definitionCN: 为获利开发土地或从地下开采矿产与能源
senses.example: The company plans to exploit the coal deposit beneath the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司计划开采山谷下的煤层。
senses.why: A mineral deposit is folded inside the earth. To exploit it is to open the ground and unfold the seam, laying out all the value it contains. This is the most literal industrial version of the Latin 'unfold'.
senses.whyCN: 矿藏折叠在地层里。exploit 就是打开地面、把矿脉摊开，把它所含的价值全部铺出来。这是拉丁语“展开”最字面的工业版本。

senses.title: Slip through a loophole in a rule
senses.definition: to take advantage of a gap or flaw in a law, rule or system
senses.definitionCN: 利用法律、规则或系统中的缺口或缺陷
senses.example: Lawyers found a way to exploit a loophole in the tax code.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们找到了钻税法空子的办法。
senses.why: A loophole is a fold or opening in a rule. Exploiting it means unfolding that opening and slipping through. The old image survives exactly: you find the weak seam and pull it open.
senses.whyCN: loophole 是规则里的一个褶缝或开口。exploit 它，就是把那个开口摊开并钻过去。古老的意象精确地保留下来：你找到薄弱的接缝，然后把它拉开。

senses.title: Turn fame or weakness into an advantage
senses.definition: to turn a personal asset or vulnerability into an advantage for yourself or others
senses.definitionCN: 把个人资产或脆弱之处转化为自己或他人的优势
senses.example: The campaign exploited her fame to raise funds.
senses.exampleCN: 这场活动利用她的名气来筹款。
senses.why: Fame, kindness and even a weakness are resources that can be unfolded for gain. The word keeps the same extractive gesture, but the material is now personal, so the tone turns colder than with 'use'.
senses.whyCN: 名气、善意甚至弱点都是可以摊开来换取利益的资源。这个词保留同一个榨取动作，但材料变成了人身，所以语气比 use 更冷。

senses.title: A bold deed: the noun sense
senses.definition: a bold, daring or impressive act, often adventurous
senses.definitionCN: 大胆、勇敢或令人赞叹的行为，常带冒险色彩
senses.example: His solo climb of the north face was a remarkable exploit.
senses.exampleCN: 他独自攀登北壁是一次了不起的壮举。
senses.why: The noun came by a different route through French: Latin explicitum meant 'something unfolded and completed', hence 'an accomplished deed'. A feat is literally a thing carried out, so the noun starts from the 'accomplished' end of the root, not the 'profitable' end.
senses.whyCN: 名词经由法语走了另一条路：拉丁语 explicitum 意为“被展开并完成的东西”，因此指“完成的功业”。壮举字面上就是“被做出来的一件事”，所以名词从词根的“完成”一端出发，而不是“获利”一端。

senses.title: A profitable use as a thing
senses.titleCN: 把“利用、开发”当作一件事
senses.definition: an act or instance of using something for profit or advantage, especially one seen as unfair
senses.definitionCN: 为利益或优势使用某物的行为，尤指被视为不公平的利用
senses.example: The report described the deal as an exploit of public trust.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把这笔交易描述为对公众信任的利用。
senses.why: Here the verb's action is frozen into a countable noun. The same unfolding is seen from outside as a thing that was done. In most modern prose this slot is filled by exploitation, and the bare noun often sounds critical.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词的动作被冻结成可数名词。同一个“摊开”从外部被看成为一件“已经做过的事”。现代文章里这个位置通常由 exploitation 填补，而光秃秃的名词常带批评口吻。

senses.title: A code attack: computing exploit
senses.definition: a piece of code or a technique that takes advantage of a software vulnerability
senses.definitionCN: 利用软件漏洞的代码或技术手段
senses.example: The hackers used a zero-day exploit to enter the network.
senses.exampleCN: 黑客利用一个零日漏洞程序进入了网络。
senses.why: The computing sense is the old metaphor made technical: a vulnerability is a fold in the code, and the exploit unfolds it and slips inside. Security jargon took the verb's 'abuse a weakness' branch and turned it into a countable tool.
senses.whyCN: 计算机义项是古老比喻的技术化：漏洞是代码里的一个褶缝，exploit 把它摊开并钻进去。安全行话取了动词“滥用弱点”这一支，把它变成一件可数的工具。

senses.title: Profit unfairly from someone's misfortune
senses.definition: to profit unfairly from someone's generosity, difficulty or misfortune
senses.definitionCN: 从他人的慷慨、困难或不幸中不公平地获利
senses.example: Some landlords exploited the housing shortage by raising rents overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一些房东利用住房短缺，一夜之间提高租金。
senses.why: The extractive gesture now has no legitimate resource behind it, only another person's difficulty. 'Full use' becomes 'unfair use', and this is where the modern negative judgement of exploit is strongest.
senses.whyCN: 这里的榨取动作背后没有正当资源，只有另一个人的困难。“充分利用”变成“不公平利用”，现代对 exploit 的负面判断在这里最强。

intro.en: Exploit is built from Latin ex- 'out' + plicare 'to fold', giving explicare 'to unfold, set out, accomplish'. The noun travelled through Old French as 'achievement', while the modern verb 'use for profit' came back through French in the 19th century. Note that plicare is 'fold', not plere 'fill' (the root behind implement).
intro.cn: exploit 由拉丁语 ex-“向外”+ plicare“折”构成，得到 explicare“展开、铺开、完成”。名词经古法语以“功绩”之义传来，而现代动词“为获利而利用”则在 19 世纪经法语回流。注意 plicare 是“折”，不是 plere“填满”（implement 的词根）。

items.en: explicare = ex- 'out' + plicare 'to fold'. The core image is unfolding something that was folded, laying it open. Its participle explicitum meant 'unfolded, set out, accomplished', which is the seed of both 'deed' and 'use'.
items.cn: explicare = ex-“向外”+ plicare“折”。核心意象是把折叠的东西展开、铺平。其分词 explicitum 意为“已展开、已铺陈、已完成”，这正是“功绩”与“利用”两义的种子。

items.en: Old French espleit / esploit meant 'achievement, profit, outcome' and came from Latin explicitum. The noun entered English around 1300 as 'deed, feat', so the earliest English exploit is a heroic act, not an abuse.
items.cn: 古法语 espleit / esploit 意为“成就、收益、结果”，来自拉丁语 explicitum。名词约在 1300 年进入英语，义为“行为、功绩”，所以英语最早的 exploit 是英雄行为，而不是滥用。

items.en: French exploiter develops the sense 'to turn to account, to work a mine or land'. The idea of extracting value grows out of the older idea of bringing a thing to completion: what is fully unfolded can be fully used.
items.cn: 法语 exploiter 发展出“加以利用、开采矿山或土地”的意思。“提取价值”的观念从更早的“把事物做到完成”生长出来：完全摊开的东西才能被完全使用。

items.en: The English verb 'to utilize for profit' is recorded in the 1830s, borrowed through French exploiter. With industrial labour the negative sense sharpens: to exploit a person is to extract their work without fair return.
items.cn: 英语动词“为获利而利用”记录于 19 世纪 30 年代，经由法语 exploiter 借入。随着工业劳动，负面含义加重：exploit 一个人，就是提取他的劳动却不给公平回报。

items.en: Computing security gives exploit a new countable noun: a program or technique that abuses a software vulnerability. The exact date of this jargon is uncertain, but the metaphor is continuous with the older 'open a weak fold and slip through'.
items.cn: 计算机安全给 exploit 一个新的可数名词义：利用软件漏洞的程序或技术。这一行话的确切年代来源不确定，但比喻与更早的“打开薄弱褶缝钻进去”一脉相承。

items.en: Exploit + -ation gives exploitation, + -er gives exploiter, + -ative gives exploitative, + -able gives exploitable; un- + exploited gives unexploited, and over- + exploit gives overexploit. The semantic chain runs unfold → accomplish → achievement → turn to account → extract value → unfair gain → code attack.
items.cn: exploit + -ation 产生 exploitation，+ -er 产生 exploiter，+ -ative 产生 exploitative，+ -able 产生 exploitable；un- + exploited 产生 unexploited，over- + exploit 产生 overexploit。语义链为：展开 → 完成 → 功绩 → 加以利用 → 提取价值 → 不公平获利 → 代码攻击。

note.en: The look-alikes share the explo-/expli- shape but split by root (plicare 'fold' vs plaudere 'clap' vs a derived noun). The near meanings differ in how neutral or how moral the 'use' is.
note.cn: 形近词共享 explo-/expli- 的外形，但词根不同（plicare“折”、plaudere“拍手”，或只是派生名词）。近义词的差别在于这种“使用”有多中性、多具道德判断。

entries.definition: the noun from exploit meaning the act of using or treating someone unfairly. It is the usual noun for the unfair sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由 exploit 派生的名词，指利用或不公平对待的行为。它是不公平义项常用的名词形式。

entries.definition: stated fully and clearly, with nothing left folded away. It comes from the same explicare 'unfold' family.
entries.definitionCN: 完整清楚地说明，没有任何东西还折着藏着。它来自同一个 explicare“展开”词族。

entries.definition: to burst outward with force. It looks close to exploit but comes from Latin plaudere 'to clap', not plicare 'to fold'.
entries.definitionCN: 向外爆裂。它看起来像 exploit，但来自拉丁语 plaudere“拍手”，而不是 plicare“折”。

entries.definition: to use something effectively for a practical purpose. It is neutral and does not imply unfairness.
entries.definitionCN: 为实际目的有效地使用某物。它中性，不含不公平的意味。

entries.definition: to use an asset or advantage to gain more than it directly gives. It is common in business talk and sounds strategic.
entries.definitionCN: 利用资产或优势获得超出其直接价值的东西。它常见于商务语境，听起来讲策略。

entries.definition: to take advantage of an opportunity or situation. It is more specific than exploit and usually less harsh.
entries.definitionCN: 利用机会或局面。它比 exploit 更具体，通常也没那么严厉。

entries.definition: to use something or someone wrongly or harmfully. It stresses the wrongdoing more than the extraction.
entries.definitionCN: 错误或有害地使用某物或某人。它比 exploit 更强调过错本身，而非榨取过程。

entries.definition: an impressive achievement. It matches the noun sense of exploit as a bold deed.
entries.definitionCN: 令人赞叹的成就。它与 exploit 名词义“壮举”相配。

normalIntro.en: These rely on the real ex- + plicare structure, the shared family with explicit, and the actual split between the 'deed' noun and the 'use' verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想依靠真实的 ex- + plicare 结构、与 explicit 共享的词族，以及“功绩”名词与“利用”动词之间的真实分裂。

normal.en: ex- = out, plicare = fold: exploit is to unfold something and lay all of it open.
normal.cn: ex- = 向外，plicare = 折：exploit 就是把某物展开、全部铺开。

normal.en: Explicit is the same family: something explicit has nothing left folded or hidden.
normal.cn: explicit 属于同一词族：显明的东西没有留下折起或藏住的部分。

normal.en: Exploit a loophole: a loophole is a fold in the law, and you pull it open.
normal.cn: exploit a loophole：漏洞是法律里的一个褶缝，你把它拉开。

normal.en: Exploit a resource or a person: the same extraction, but the second is morally judged.
normal.cn: exploit a resource 与 exploit a person：同样是榨取，但后者受道德评判。

normal.en: The noun exploit comes from the 'completed deed' side, which is why it can still mean a heroic feat.
normal.cn: 名词 exploit 来自“已完成的功业”这一侧，所以它至今仍可指英雄壮举。

abstract.en: Picture a folded map. Opening it fully is the original gesture; using every road on it is the modern meaning.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折叠的地图。把它完全打开是最初的动作；把上面每条路都用上，则是现代的含义。

abstract.en: The same gesture can open a mine, a legal loophole, a person's kindness or a line of code.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作可以打开一座矿、一条法律空子、一个人的善意，或一行代码。

abstract.en: The word's history splits at the end: 'a deed completed' becomes the noun feat, while 'value fully extracted' becomes the verb exploit.
abstract.cn: 这个词的历史在末端分叉：“被完成的功业”成为名词壮举，而“被彻底提取的价值”成为动词利用。

examples.en: The company was fined for exploiting cheap labour abroad.
examples.cn: 这家公司因剥削海外廉价劳动力而被罚款。

examples.en: We should exploit this window of good weather to finish the roof.
examples.cn: 我们应当利用这段好天气把屋顶修完。

examples.en: The climb was one of the great exploits of the decade.
examples.cn: 那次攀登是那个十年最伟大的壮举之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一扑就捞”——看见机会就扑上去捞一把 → exploit 利用、占便宜

root: 拉丁 explicare = ex-“向外”+ plicare“折”，字面“展开、铺开”，引申为“做到完成、加以利用”；名词经古法语 esploit“成就”而来。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of exploit all start from one gesture: unfolding something completely. Applied to land, ore, rules, fame or code it means extracting value; applied to a completed act it becomes a feat; applied to another person's need it becomes unfair gain.
sensesIntro.cn: exploit 的九个义项都从同一个动作出发：把某物彻底摊开。作用于土地、矿石、规则、名气或代码时，它是提取价值；作用于一件已完成的行为时，它是壮举；作用于他人的困境时，它是不公平获利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded thing is opened out flat, and every part of it is used.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件折着的东西被摊平，它的每一部分都被用上。

branches.en: RESOURCES: forests, land and mineral seams are unfolded and worked for profit.
branches.cn: 资源：森林、土地和矿脉被摊开并加以开采获利。

branches.en: PEOPLE: when the thing being extracted is human work or human need, extraction becomes exploitation and unfair gain.
branches.cn: 人：当被提取的是人的劳动或人的困境时，提取就变成剥削与不公平获利。

branches.en: WEAKNESSES: a loophole, a famous name or a personal weakness is pried open and used.
branches.cn: 弱点：法律空子、名气或个人的软肋被撬开并利用。

branches.en: THE NOUN: the completed-deed side becomes a feat, while the profitable-use side becomes a countable act of using.
branches.cn: 名词：完成功业的一侧成为壮举，而获利使用的一侧成为可数的利用行为。

branches.en: CODE: a software vulnerability is a fold in code, and the exploit opens it and slips inside.
branches.cn: 代码：软件漏洞是代码里的褶缝，exploit 把它打开并钻进去。

intro.en: Exploit is a Latin verb stem with the prefix ex- already attached. English adds its own noun, adjective and verb suffixes; the prefix inside the word is no longer felt as a separate piece.
intro.cn: exploit 是一个已经带上前缀 ex- 的拉丁动词词干。英语再附加自己的名词、形容词和动词后缀；词内的前缀已不再被感觉为独立成分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on plicare 'to fold': explicare 'to unfold', explicitus 'unfolded, clear', explicatio 'an unfolding, explanation'. The unrelated plere 'to fill' belongs to a different family, which is why implement and exploit must not be confused.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族建立在 plicare“折”上：explicare“展开”、explicitus“展开的、清楚的”、explicatio“展开、解释”。不相干的 plere“填满”属于另一个词族，所以 implement 与 exploit 不能混为一谈。

items.meaning: the act of using resources or treating people unfairly for profit
items.meaningCN: 剥削；利用；开发（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: The report documented the exploitation of seasonal workers.
items.exampleCN: 报告记录了季节工遭受剥削的情况。

items.meaning: a person or group that exploits others
items.meaningCN: 剥削者；利用者（-er 表示做该动作的人或组织）
items.example: The tenants called the landlord an exploiter.
items.exampleCN: 房客们称这个房东是剥削者。

items.meaning: tending to take unfair advantage of people
items.meaningCN: 剥削性的；利用性的（-ative 构成倾向形容词）
items.example: They worked under exploitative conditions.
items.exampleCN: 他们在剥削性的条件下工作。

items.meaning: able to be used or taken advantage of
items.meaningCN: 可利用的；可开发的（-able 表示“能被……”）
items.example: The flaw is exploitable by anyone with basic skills.
items.exampleCN: 任何具备基础技能的人都能利用这个漏洞。

items.meaning: not yet developed or used
items.meaningCN: 未被开发的；未利用的（un- 表否定）
items.example: The country has vast unexploited gas reserves.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家拥有大量未开发的天然气储量。

items.meaning: to use a resource beyond what it can sustain
items.meaningCN: 过度开发；过度利用（over- 表过度）
items.example: Fisheries that overexploit their stocks eventually collapse.
items.exampleCN: 过度捕捞的渔场最终会崩溃。

items.meaning: excessive use of a resource beyond sustainable limits
items.meaningCN: 过度开发；过度利用（over- 加 -ation）
items.example: Overexploitation of groundwater is sinking the city.
items.exampleCN: 地下水的过度开采正在让这座城市下沉。

items.meaning: the quality of being able to be exploited
items.meaningCN: 可利用性；可剥削性（-ability 构成能力名词）
items.example: Researchers rated the exploitability of each bug.
items.exampleCN: 研究人员评估了每个漏洞的可利用性。

latinEntries.meaning: to unfold, set out, explain, accomplish

latinEntries.meaningCN: 已展开的；清楚的；完整陈述的

definition_en: to travel through an unfamiliar area, or to examine a subject, possibility or set of data, in order to learn about it
core_image: 举着火把走进没有地图的洞穴：边走、边喊、边看、边记
scene: The team used a small robot to explore the flooded cave before anyone entered.
sceneCN: 这里 explore 是「到陌生地方考察」（第 1 个义项：进入不熟悉的地方以了解它）；句意：在任何人进入之前，团队先用一个小机器人探索被水淹没的洞穴。图中可辨识物件：机器人、头灯、被水淹没的洞穴、绳索、洞穴地图。

pos.zh: 勘探；探查（资源、身体内部）

senses.title: Travel through an unfamiliar place
senses.definition: to travel through an unfamiliar area in order to learn about it
senses.definitionCN: 穿过不熟悉的地区以了解它
senses.example: They spent the summer exploring the islands by boat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整个夏天乘船探索这些岛屿。
senses.why: Latin explorare began as a hunting word: the shout that drives game out and tells the hunter where it is. Walking into an unknown region repeats that gesture — you call into the unknown and follow whatever answers.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 explorare 起初是狩猎词：喊声把猎物驱赶出来，也告诉猎人它在哪。走进未知地区重复了这个动作——你对着未知喊一声，然后跟着回应走。

senses.title: Examine possibilities before deciding
senses.definition: to examine a subject or a range of possibilities carefully, especially before making a choice
senses.definitionCN: 仔细考察一个主题或一系列可能性，尤在作选择之前
senses.example: We are still exploring options for the new office.
senses.exampleCN: 我们还在探讨新办公室的各种选择。
senses.why: Once 'search out' moved from animals to questions, exploring options means flushing out every possibility before choosing. The hunter's shout becomes a question put to the future, and no answer is fixed yet.
senses.whyCN: 一旦“搜出”从动物转向问题，explore options 就意为在决定前把每种可能性都轰出来。猎人的喊声变成投向未来的问题，而答案尚未固定。

senses.title: Explore space
senses.definition: to investigate space, planets or other celestial bodies with probes or crewed missions
senses.definitionCN: 用探测器或载人任务考察太空、行星或其他天体
senses.example: Robots will explore the moon's south pole before astronauts return.
senses.exampleCN: 在宇航员重返之前，机器人将先探索月球南极。
senses.why: The same ex- 'out' and plorare 'cry' are scaled to the sky: instruments are sent outward to search where no one has called before. Space is simply the largest unfamiliar hunting ground the word has been asked to cover.
senses.whyCN: 同样的 ex-“向外”与 plorare“呼喊”被放大到天空：仪器被送出去，搜索无人呼喊过的地方。太空只是这个词被要求覆盖的最大一片陌生猎场。

senses.title: Explore data for patterns
senses.definition: to examine a set of data systematically in order to find patterns, outliers or anomalies
senses.definitionCN: 系统地考察一组数据，以寻找模式、离群值或异常
senses.example: Analysts explore the dataset before they build a model.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师在建模之前会先探查数据集。
senses.why: Data has no landscape, but the method is the same: probe the set from many angles until hidden patterns answer. 'Explore' marks open-ended search before a model commits to an answer.
senses.whyCN: 数据没有地形，但方法相同：从多个角度探查数据集，直到隐藏的模式作出回应。explore 标记的是在模型给出答案之前的开放式搜索。

senses.title: Explore one's feelings
senses.definition: to examine one's own feelings or inner life, often slowly and with care
senses.definitionCN: 考察自己的情绪或内心世界，常缓慢而谨慎
senses.example: Therapy gave her a safe place to explore her grief.
senses.exampleCN: 心理治疗给了她一个安全的地方去探索自己的悲伤。
senses.why: The search turns inward: feelings are treated as terrain to be walked over rather than conclusions to be announced. The word's open, non-committal search suits therapy's slow uncovering.
senses.whyCN: 搜索转向内部：情绪被当作可以走一遍的地形，而不是需要宣布的结论。这个词开放、不急着下判断的搜索方式，正好适合治疗中缓慢的揭示。

senses.title: Investigate an academic topic
senses.definition: to investigate a topic or question systematically in academic work
senses.definitionCN: 在学术工作中系统地考察一个主题或问题
senses.example: The paper explores the causes of the revolt.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文探讨这场起义的起因。
senses.why: Academic explore keeps the 'search out causes' core of explorare: a paper explores when it opens a question and follows it, rather than proving one pre-set point.
senses.whyCN: 学术用法的 explore 保留了 explorare“搜出原因”的核心：论文 explore 一个课题，是打开一个问题并跟着它走，而不是证明一个预设结论。

senses.title: Search an area for resources
senses.definition: to search an area for mineral, oil or gas resources
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地区寻找矿产、石油或天然气资源
senses.example: The company is exploring for oil off the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司正在近海勘探石油。
senses.why: This is the most literal modern descendant: geologists search an area, sending surveys out until the ground answers. ex- 'out' still marks the movement outward from known ground into unproven ground.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的现代后裔：地质学家搜索一片区域，把勘探信号送出去，直到大地作出回应。ex-“向外”仍标记着从已知地面走向未证实地面的动作。

senses.title: Surgical exploration
senses.definition: to examine an internal part of the body, often surgically, in order to find the cause of a problem
senses.definitionCN: 常通过手术检查身体内部，以找出病因
senses.example: The surgeon decided to perform an exploratory operation.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生决定做一次探查性手术。
senses.why: Surgical exploration opens the body to search for the cause, which is 'search out' in its oldest medical form. The procedure is called exploratory because it looks before it acts.
senses.whyCN: 医学探查打开身体以寻找病因，这是“搜出”最古老的医学形态。这种手术叫 exploratory，因为它先看，再动手。

senses.title: Put an idea forward tentatively
senses.definition: to raise or consider an idea tentatively, without committing to it
senses.definitionCN: 试探性地提出或考虑一个想法，并不承诺采纳
senses.example: She explored the idea of moving abroad during the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她在会上试探性地提出了移居国外的想法。
senses.why: To explore an idea is to send out a tentative probe without landing on it: the cry goes out, but no claim is made. This is the softened, social end of the 'search out' chain.
senses.whyCN: explore 一个想法，是发出一次试探性的探测而不落地：喊声出去了，但不作任何断言。这是“搜出”链条最柔和、最社交化的一端。

intro.en: Explore comes from Latin explorare 'to investigate, search out'. The usual analysis is ex- 'out' + plorare 'to cry out', a hunting image, but this composition is not certain. English first uses it for investigation in the 1580s and for travel into unknown regions in the 1610s, then extends it to space, data, feelings and medicine.
intro.cn: explore 来自拉丁语 explorare“调查、搜出”。通行分析是 ex-“向外”+ plorare“呼喊”，即狩猎意象，但这一构成并不确定。英语 1580 年代先用它表示“调查”，1610 年代用于“进入未知地区考察”，之后再扩展到太空、数据、情感和医学。

items.en: explorare meant 'to investigate, search out', and in classical military use also 'to spy out'. Its frequent participle exploratus gave the noun explorator 'scout, investigator'.
items.cn: explorare 意为“调查、搜出”，在古典军事用法里也指“侦察”。其分词 exploratus 产生名词 explorator“侦察者、调查者”。

items.en: The word is generally analysed as ex- 'out' + plorare 'to cry out'. The image is a hunter shouting to drive game from cover. Some reference works mark the composition as uncertain, and plorare itself also means 'to wail'; the hunting explanation is plausible but not proven.
items.cn: 这个词一般被分析为 ex-“向外”+ plorare“呼喊”。意象是猎人喊叫把猎物从藏身处赶出来。部分资料把这一构成标为不确定，而 plorare 本身也有“哀号”之义；狩猎解释合理，但未被证实。

items.en: English records explore in the 1580s with the sense 'to investigate, examine'. The word arrives through French explorer, which itself continues the Latin verb.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 80 年代记录到 explore，义为“调查、审查”。这个词经由法语 explorer 传入，而法语又延续了拉丁动词。

items.en: From the 1610s explore means 'to travel into unknown regions in order to discover them'. The physical journey sense separates from the mental examination sense, and both survive.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪 10 年代起，explore 表示“进入未知地区以发现它们”。身体旅行的义项与心智考察的义项分开，两者都保留下来。

items.en: Exploration becomes the standard noun for voyages of discovery, and explorer the standard noun for the person. In the 20th century the word extends to space exploration, data exploration and exploratory surgery, so the 'search out' core now covers any unknown terrain.
items.cn: exploration 成为“发现之旅”的标准名词，explorer 成为“探索者”的标准名词。20 世纪，这个词扩展到太空探索、数据探索和探查性手术，于是“搜出”的核心现在覆盖任何未知领域。

items.en: Explore + -er gives explorer, + -ation gives exploration, + -atory gives exploratory, + -ative gives explorative. Un- + explored gives unexplored, re- + explore gives re-explore, and under- + explored gives underexplored. The suffix chain marks person, process, manner and degree, all still attached to the same outward search.
items.cn: explore + -er 产生 explorer，+ -ation 产生 exploration，+ -atory 产生 exploratory，+ -ative 产生 explorative。un- + explored 产生 unexplored，re- + explore 产生 re-explore，under- + explored 产生 underexplored。后缀链标记人、过程、方式与程度，全部仍附着在同一个向外的搜索上。

note.en: The look-alikes share the explo- opening but differ by root; the near meanings range from neutral searching to formal examination and physical probing.
note.cn: 形近词共享 explo- 开头但词根不同；近义词则从中性的搜索，到正式的审查，再到身体性的探查。

entries.definition: the noun from explore: the act or process of searching an area or a subject. It is not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: explore 派生的名词：探索地区或考察主题的行为或过程。它不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: to use something or someone for profit. It looks close but comes from plicare 'to fold', not plorare 'to cry out'.
entries.definitionCN: 为获利使用某物或某人。它看起来相近，但来自 plicare“折”，而不是 plorare“呼喊”。

entries.definition: to burst outward with force. It shares the ex- opening but comes from Latin plaudere 'to clap'.
entries.definitionCN: 向外爆裂。它共享 ex- 开头，但来自拉丁语 plaudere“拍手”。

entries.definition: to examine a crime, problem or claim officially and systematically. It is narrower and more institutional than explore.
entries.definitionCN: 正式、系统地调查犯罪、问题或说法。它比 explore 更窄、更带机构色彩。

entries.definition: to look over a whole area or situation to get an overall picture. It stresses coverage rather than open-ended discovery.
entries.definitionCN: 巡视整个地区或局面以获得全貌。它强调覆盖范围，而非开放式发现。

entries.definition: to investigate something closely, often something hidden or sensitive. It is more pointed and physical than explore.
entries.definitionCN: 近距离调查某物，尤指隐藏或敏感之事。它比 explore 更有针对性、更身体化。

entries.definition: to look carefully for something lost or wanted. It has a clear target, while explore is open-ended.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细寻找丢失或想要的东西。它有明确目标，而 explore 是开放式的。

entries.definition: to look at something in detail in order to judge or understand it. It is more evaluative than explore.
entries.definitionCN: 为判断或理解而细看某物。它比 explore 更具评估性。

normalIntro.en: These use the real ex- + plorare analysis, the hunting image that is plausible but not certain, and the true noun family of explorer and exploration.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想使用真实的 ex- + plorare 分析、合理但未被证实的狩猎意象，以及 explorer、exploration 的真实名词词族。

normal.en: ex- = out, plorare = cry out: explore is to call outward into the unknown.
normal.cn: ex- = 向外，plorare = 呼喊：explore 就是对着未知向外喊一声。

normal.en: The hunter's shout both startles the game and tells the hunter where it is, which is why 'cry out' could become 'search out'.
normal.cn: 猎人的喊声既惊动猎物，也告诉猎人它在哪，所以“呼喊”能变成“搜出”。

normal.en: Explorer, exploration and exploratory keep the same outward search under different suffixes.
normal.cn: explorer、exploration、exploratory 用不同后缀保留同一个向外的搜索。

normal.en: Explore options means calling out every possibility before you choose one.
normal.cn: explore options 意为在选择之前把每种可能性都喊出来。

normal.en: Space exploration is the same word scaled up: instruments call out where no one has called before.
normal.cn: space exploration 是同一个词的放大版：仪器在无人呼喊过的地方发出呼叫。

abstract.en: Picture a torch entering a cave with no map. The beam moves, the voice echoes, and the map is drawn as you go.
abstract.cn: 想象一支火把进入没有地图的洞穴。光束移动，声音回响，地图边走边画。

abstract.en: Sometimes you shout and wait for an echo; sometimes you probe quietly. Explore covers both the loud search and the careful examination.
abstract.cn: 有时你喊一声等待回声；有时你安静地探查。explore 同时覆盖大声搜索与仔细考察。

abstract.en: The word's outside and inside are the same: the cave, the dataset, the feeling and the body are all terrain to be searched.
abstract.cn: 这个词的外与内是一回事：洞穴、数据集、情感和身体，都是可供搜索的地形。

examples.en: We spent the afternoon exploring the old town on foot.
examples.cn: 我们花了一下午步行探索老城。

examples.en: The committee will explore whether a cheaper plan is possible.
examples.cn: 委员会将探讨是否有可能制定一个更便宜的方案。

examples.en: Geologists are exploring the region for copper.
examples.cn: 地质学家正在该地区勘探铜矿。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一颗思路，扑向路径”——带着一颗思路扑向未知的路 → explore 探索、探究

root: 拉丁 explorare“调查、搜出”，一般分析为 ex-“向外”+ plorare“呼喊”（猎人驱赶猎物的喊声，构成来源不确定）；核心是“向外搜索、把未知找出来”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of explore all share one outward search: a shout into the unknown that becomes a journey, a question, a probe of data, a walk through feelings, a survey of ground, an operation, or a tentative idea.
sensesIntro.cn: explore 的九个义项都共享同一次向外的搜索：一声对未知的呼喊，可以变成旅程、问题、对数据的探查、对情感的走访、对地面的勘探、一次手术，或一个试探性的想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice or beam goes out into an unknown space and the answer is followed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束声音或光射入未知空间，然后跟着回应走。

branches.en: PLACES: an unfamiliar region, outer space and the ground under survey are all physical terrain searched outward.
branches.cn: 地方：陌生地区、外太空和被勘探的地面，都是向外搜索的物理地形。

branches.en: POSSIBILITIES: options and tentative ideas are possibilities called out before any choice is fixed.
branches.cn: 可能性：选项和试探性的想法，都是在作出选择之前被喊出来的可能性。

branches.en: DATA: the search becomes systematic probing of a dataset for patterns and anomalies.
branches.cn: 数据：搜索变成对数据集的系统探查，寻找模式与异常。

branches.en: INNER LIFE: the beam turns inward and feelings become terrain to be walked over slowly.
branches.cn: 内心：光束转向内部，情感成为需要慢慢走一遍的地形。

branches.en: INVESTIGATION: academic research and surgical exploration both search out a cause before acting.
branches.cn: 调查：学术研究与医学探查都在行动之前先搜出原因。

intro.en: Explore is a Latin verb stem with ex- already inside it. English adds -er, -ation, -atory and -ative to name the person, the process, the manner and the tendency; un-, re- and under- adjust the scope.
intro.cn: explore 是一个内部已含 ex- 的拉丁动词词干。英语加 -er、-ation、-atory、-ative 来命名人、过程、方式与倾向；un-、re-、under- 调整范围。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is explorare 'to search out', explorator 'scout', exploratio 'investigation', and plorare 'to cry out'. The last link is the uncertain one, which is why the hunting image is offered as probable rather than certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族包括 explorare“搜出”、explorator“侦察者”、exploratio“调查”，以及 plorare“呼喊”。最后一环正是不确定的部分，所以狩猎意象只能作为“可能”而非“确定”提出。

items.meaning: a person who travels to unfamiliar places to learn about them
items.meaningCN: 探险者；探索者（-er 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The explorer spent a month mapping the river.
items.exampleCN: 这位探险者花了一个月绘制那条河的地图。

items.meaning: the act or process of exploring
items.meaningCN: 探索；勘探；探究（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: Oil exploration has been paused for the winter.
items.exampleCN: 石油勘探在冬季暂停了。

items.meaning: having the nature of exploring; investigative
items.meaningCN: 探索性的；探究性的（-ative 构成倾向形容词）
items.example: The course takes an explorative approach to history.
items.exampleCN: 这门课对历史采取探索式的教学方法。

items.meaning: done in order to find out something before acting
items.meaningCN: 探查性的；探索性的（-atory 表示目的）
items.example: They began with an exploratory study.
items.exampleCN: 他们从一项探索性研究开始。

items.meaning: in a way that is intended to find something out
items.meaningCN: 以探查的方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The team acted exploratorily before committing funds.
items.exampleCN: 团队在投入资金前先做了探查性行动。

items.meaning: not yet travelled through or examined
items.meaningCN: 未探索的；未勘探的（un- 表否定）
items.example: Much of the ocean floor remains unexplored.
items.exampleCN: 大部分海底仍未被探索。

items.meaning: to explore a place or subject again
items.meaningCN: 重新探索；再次考察（re- 表再次）
items.example: The book re-explores a familiar story from a new angle.
items.exampleCN: 这本书从新角度重新探讨一个熟悉的故事。

items.meaning: examined less than it deserves
items.meaningCN: 研究不足的；探索不充分的（under- 表不足）
items.example: The topic remains underexplored in the literature.
items.exampleCN: 这个课题在文献中仍未得到充分研究。

latinEntries.structure: ex- (out) + plorare (cry out), though the analysis is not fully certain
latinEntries.meaning: to investigate, search out, spy out
